appStores.title: App Sources
appStores.description: Manage where CasaNova pulls its app catalog from. Multiple sources merge into one catalog, ordered by priority (lower number wins on conflicts).
appStores.how_desc: Each enabled source contributes apps to the unified Library catalog. When two sources offer the same app, the one with the lower priority number takes precedence. Disable a source to hide its apps without removing it.
appStores.compat_note: The CasaOS App Store is the default community catalog, kept for compatibility with the wider CasaOS ecosystem. Leave it enabled to keep the familiar app selection.
appStores.add_desc: Point CasaNova at a remote app-store URL (a CasaOS-compatible store index). The server validates the URL before adding it.
appStores.confirm_delete: Remove app source '{name}'? Its apps will no longer appear in the Library.

theme_packs.title: Theme packs
theme_packs.subtitle: Upload custom UI themes as .zip packages. Each pack supplies a tokens.css and optional asset images that override the bundled look.
theme_packs.upload_desc: Pick a .zip on your computer. The pack must contain a theme.json (with id + name) and a tokens.css. Optional assets/ folder is served at /v1/sys/themes/{id}/assets/.
theme_packs.upload_hint: Maximum 16 MB. Existing packs with the same id are replaced atomically.
theme_packs.empty: No packs installed yet. Upload one above.

remote_access.title: Remote access
remote_access.subtitle: Reach this server from outside your LAN. CasaNova detects whichever connectors are installed and reports their status.
remote_access.intro_body: CasaNova doesn't bundle a remote-access vendor. Pick the one that fits your network: Tailscale for a personal mesh VPN, Cloudflare Tunnel for public HTTPS over your own domain, ZeroTier for SDN-style virtual LAN. Each connector is independent — you can run more than one.

migration.status_pending: Migration detected — review and acknowledge when ready.
migration.configs_desc: These configs were copied into /etc/casanova/ at install time and are read by the running services.
migration.compose_desc: Stacks discovered in {dir}. CasaNova reads from the same path as upstream CasaOS — no changes needed.
migration.containers_count: {n} container(s) carry the upstream casaos=casaos label and remain in the dashboard.
migration.units_desc: casaos-* units detected. The installer disabled the ones it knew about; active or enabled units here would clash with CasaNova.

general.description: Language, theme, and basic system info.
general.language_desc: The language used throughout the CasaNova dashboard.
general.theme_desc: Mode, accent color, transparency, and wallpapers. Changes apply instantly.
general.theme_variant_desc: Overlays a visual personality on top of your accent + mode picks. Upload your own theme packs from Appearance → Theme packs.
general.transparency_desc: Frosted-glass effect on floating cards. Lets the wallpaper peek through.
general.icon_pack_desc: Switch the icon style across the interface, including folders and file types. Phosphor offers duotone and fill variants.
general.app_icon_style_desc: Choose how app icons look on the dashboard. "Traditional" shows the logo without the colored tile.
general.file_icon_style_desc: "Line" follows the chosen icon pack; "Classic" uses filled, colorful icons (traditional yellow folder, disk, etc.).
general.icon_accent_desc: Applies to the line folder & file icons. "Default" colors each by type; an accent tints them all alike.
general.icon_glow_desc: Adds a soft halo in the icon's color.
general.replicate_bg_desc: Use the same wallpaper behind the floating cards on every settings and file-manager page.
general.dev_mode_desc: Reveal experimental features and not-yet-finished surfaces across the dashboard.
general.dev_mode_off: Off — only production-ready features are shown.
general.advanced_mode_on: On — destructive lifecycle actions unlocked (zpool create / destroy / replace).
general.advanced_mode_off: Off — destructive actions hidden. Recommended for everyday use.
general.search_engine_desc: Used by the search bar on the dashboard. Opens in a new tab.
general.dashboard_tips_desc: Onboarding hints shown at the top of the dashboard.
general.dashboard_tips_off: Hidden — the dashboard starts with the search bar.

about.title: About CasaNova
about.repair_confirm: Reinstall the current version's system files from the cached package? Services will restart. This repairs corrupted files without changing your version or data.
about.clear_cache_confirm: Remove the cached update package? This frees disk space. You'll need to re-stage it to repair from cache later.
about.credits_desc: CasaNova stands on the shoulders of these projects. Thank you.
about.system_update_desc: Applies to CasaNova core services, dashboard, and migrations.
about.rollback_confirm: Roll back to the previous build? Services will restart.
about.fixture_mode_warning: Running in offline demo mode — actions are simulated.

about.disk_update_invalid_file: File must be a .tar.gz or .tgz archive.

troubleshooter.title: Troubleshooter
troubleshooter.description: Diagnose and fix common issues with your server.
troubleshooter.network_repair_desc: Restarts Docker to recreate NAT/firewall rules. Fixes containers that can't reach the internet.
troubleshooter.fix_docker_network_detail: Restarts the Docker daemon, which recreates iptables MASQUERADE rules. Containers will briefly stop and restart.
troubleshooter.restart_gateway_desc: Restarts the CasaNova gateway. The dashboard will disconnect for a few seconds.
troubleshooter.restart_all_desc: Restarts every CasaNova service in the correct order. Use this when multiple things seem broken.
troubleshooter.flush_dns_desc: Clears the system DNS cache. Helps when domain names aren't resolving.
troubleshooter.service_management_desc: Restart individual services or the entire CasaNova stack.
troubleshooter.confirm_message: Run "{action}"? Some services will be temporarily unavailable.
troubleshooter.confirm_restart_all: This will restart ALL CasaNova services. The dashboard will disconnect and reconnect automatically.
troubleshooter.confirm_docker: This will restart Docker. All containers will briefly stop and restart. Are you sure?

users.title: Users & Roles
users.description: Manage accounts, roles, and permissions across CasaNova.
users.delete_confirm: Are you sure you want to delete {name}? This can't be undone.
users.roles_reference_desc: What each role is allowed to do across the dashboard.

errors.last_admin: You can't remove or demote the last administrator.
errors.duplicate: A user with that name already exists.

wizard.launcher_desc: Guided flow to format, mount, and optionally pool a fresh set of drives.
wizard.welcome_body_1: Let's get your disks ready for apps. The wizard formats fresh drives as ext4 and mounts them under /DATA, where every CasaNova app expects to find its persistent storage.
wizard.welcome_body_2: If you have more than one disk, you can optionally pool them with MergerFS so they appear as a single drive — files transparently land on whichever member has space.
wizard.pick_instructions: Select the disks you want to set up. Already-mounted disks and USB sticks are hidden so you can't accidentally wipe one.
wizard.no_disks: No eligible disks found. Plug in fresh drives and reopen this wizard.
wizard.layout_intro: Pick a layout for the selected disks.
wizard.layout_single_desc: Each disk gets its own mount point at /DATA/diskN.
wizard.layout_pool_desc: Combine all selected disks into one big /DATA — easy to grow later.
wizard.no_raid_note: RAID mirroring isn't offered here. CasaNova prefers MergerFS for pooling because it tolerates uneven disk sizes and lets you remove a member without rebuilding. Use the per-disk controls below the wizard if you need mdadm.
wizard.apply_success: Drives are ready. You can close this wizard.

storage.title: Storage
storage.description: Disks, mounts, SMART health, and merged storage.
storage.standby_desc: Spin down idle hard disks to save power and extend their lifespan.
storage.standby_off_hint: Disks stay spinning at all times.
storage.standby_on_hint: Rotational disks will spin down after {n} min of inactivity.
storage.format_warning: Formatting {device} will erase all data on the disk. This cannot be undone.
storage.zfs_desc: Pools, scrub, snapshots. Lights up automatically when zfsutils-linux is installed on the host.
storage.zfs_install_hint: Install zfsutils-linux on the host and reload to manage pools from here.
storage.zfs_no_pools_hint: Create a pool, or import one with sudo zpool import <name>.
storage.zfs_export_confirm: Export pool {pool}? Open files on the pool must be closed first.
storage.zfs_no_unmounted: No unmounted disks. Format or unmount a disk first.
storage.zfs_destroy_warning: Destroying pool {pool} permanently erases every dataset, every snapshot. There is no undo.
storage.zfs_replace_desc: Replace {old} in pool {pool} with a new device. ZFS will resilver onto the new disk.
storage.resize_description: Grow {device} to use all the space on its block device. Online resize — no unmount needed.
storage.benchmark_description: Run a sequential + random IO test on {device}. Writes a temporary scratch file under the mount point.
storage.merge_description: Add {device} to a storage pool. For now this opens the pool wizard — pool selection comes in a follow-up.
storage.smart_desc: Self-Monitoring, Analysis and Reporting Technology status for connected drives
storage.smart_no_smartctl: smartctl is not installed. Install smartmontools to enable disk health monitoring.
storage.smart_schedule_desc: Automatically run SMART self-tests on a schedule
storage.zfs_snapshots_desc: Create, manage, and rollback ZFS filesystem snapshots
storage.zfs_snapshot_no_zfs: ZFS is not available on this system
storage.zfs_snapshot_rollback_warning: This will revert the dataset to its state at the time of the snapshot. All changes made after this snapshot will be lost. Type the snapshot name to confirm:
storage.zfs_snapshot_delete_warning: This will permanently delete the snapshot. This cannot be undone.

network.https_desc: Automatic certificates via Let's Encrypt, or self-signed fallback for .local domains.
network.https_hint: Serve the dashboard over TLS on port 443.
network.test_renewal_running: Talking to ACME staging — no changes will be saved.

host.title: Host & Tuning
host.description: Administer the Linux underneath CasaNova — CPU, memory, storage, sensors and services.
host.gov_desc: How the CPU trades power for performance. 'performance' locks max clocks; 'powersave' minimises them; 'ondemand'/'schedutil' scale with load.
host.gov_unsupported: CPU frequency scaling is not available on this system (common under virtualization).
host.swap_desc: How eagerly the kernel swaps memory to disk (0–100). Lower keeps more in RAM — good for a NAS with plenty of memory.
host.mem_desc: Cap the RAM the Docker stack may use (e.g. 4G, 512M). Applied live; the CasaNova management stack is never limited so the UI stays reachable.
host.apt_desc: Check for and install operating-system package updates. Checking is read-only; upgrading applies every available update.
host.apt_unsupported: This system does not use APT.
host.apt_reboot: A reboot is required to finish applying earlier updates.
host.apt_count: No updates available | 1 update available | {n} updates available
host.apt_stale: package lists could not be refreshed
host.apt_confirm_body: This will install all {n} available package updates. It runs in the background and continues even if CasaNova restarts.
host.apt_confirm_docker: This update touches Docker, containerd, or the kernel — running containers may restart and a reboot may be needed.
host.zram_desc: A compressed swap device in RAM — faster than disk swap and saves the SSD. Good on a box with spare CPU.
host.io_desc: How the kernel orders disk requests. bfq suits spinning HDDs; none/mq-deadline suit SSDs and NVMe. Also sets read-ahead.
host.svc_desc: Restart or toggle key host services. SSH is restart-only so you can never lock yourself out from here.
host.ups_desc: Battery backup status — local, or from a remote NUT server on your network.
host.ups_none: No UPS detected. Configure a remote NUT server if yours runs on another host.
host.ups_remote_desc: Query a remote NUT (upsd) server. Leave the host empty to use a local UPS.
host.power_desc: UPS-aware power management. Reads the Forza power daemon and, when enabled, runs an ordered shutdown before the battery dies.
host.power_enable_desc: When off, UPS state is only observed — nothing touches the box.
host.power_autoshutdown_desc: On a confirmed shutdown_now, stop apps in order and power off.
host.power_forza_token_desc: Optional. Paste the Forza daemon's api_token to report this box's draw/mode back to Forza (topology + Wake-on-LAN). Leave empty to only read UPS state.
host.power_unreachable: Forza power daemon not reachable. Check the URL and that the daemon is running.
host.power_essential_apps_desc: Container names stopped LAST during an ordered shutdown (databases). Comma-separated; also excluded from pausing.
host.power_ladder_desc: On battery (prepare_shutdown): CPU governor to powersave, EPP to power, spin down the disks below. Reverts when mains power returns.
host.power_spindown_disks_desc: Kernel names of non-critical spinning disks (e.g. sda) sent to standby on battery. Any access wakes them. Empty = skip.
host.power_pause_apps_desc: docker-pause every non-essential app while on battery (freezes them — remote access through paused apps drops). Unpaused when power returns.
host.proc_desc: Highest memory processes (read-only). Container-owned processes are managed from Apps.
host.sysctl_desc: A curated set of sysctls. Only touch these if you know what they do.
host.apt_repo_failed: {n} repository could not be refreshed ({repo}) | {n} repositories could not be refreshed ({repo}, …)

maintenance.empty_title: Nothing to reclaim. The system is clean.
maintenance.truncated_note: Showing the first {shown} of {total}. The full list is written to the manifest on disk.

maintenance.reason_stale_scan: The analysis expired. Analyze again before deleting.

maintenance.cat_update_packages_hint: Release tarballs older than the version installed.
maintenance.cat_update_packages_consequence: You lose the ability to reinstall those versions without an internet connection.
maintenance.cat_upgrade_backups_hint: Upgrade backups superseded by a newer one.
maintenance.cat_upgrade_backups_consequence: The rollback for those upgrades goes away. The most recent backup is never offered here.
maintenance.cat_rotated_logs_hint: Rotated log files no process is writing to.
maintenance.cat_rotated_logs_consequence: Old log history is gone. The live log and the audit log are not touched.
maintenance.cat_orphan_journal_hint: systemd journal belonging to an older machine-id.
maintenance.cat_orphan_journal_consequence: You lose the system journal of the previous install. The current journal is not touched.
maintenance.cat_apt_cache_hint: Packages apt downloaded and has already installed.
maintenance.cat_apt_cache_consequence: apt downloads them again if it ever needs to reinstall one.
maintenance.cat_scratch_hint: Chunk and upload scratch left behind by interrupted transfers.
maintenance.cat_scratch_consequence: Interrupted uploads and copies can no longer be resumed.
maintenance.notice_docker_volumes_why: Docker does not know which app each one came from. "Unused" only means no container references it right now — and stopping an app removes its containers, so every app you switched off is on that list. Uninstalling an app is where its volumes get offered.
maintenance.notice_docker_stopped_why: These are apps you turned off, not junk. Removing them loses the writable layer and makes the project disappear from compose, which is the "installed but offline" bug we already fixed once.
maintenance.notice_docker_tagged_why: These are the previous versions of your apps: the rollback. This box has already been left without internet while the LAN was fine, and an image deleted with no way to pull it again is a dead app.
maintenance.notice_docker_overlay2_why: That is the size of the tree, not what could be reclaimed. The layer mapping is Docker's internal business and changes between versions; dockerd is its only legitimate owner.
maintenance.notice_appdata_why: "No app installed" also describes someone who uninstalled an app to reinstall it and expects to find their files again. Browse it yourself and decide.
maintenance.notice_in_use_label: Images, volumes and data in use
maintenance.notice_in_use_why: This is what makes the system work.
maintenance.notice_user_caches_why: It belongs to a user account, not to the system. The owner already has the tools to clear it.
maintenance.notice_trash_why: The trash is the undo layer of a different feature, with 30 days of retention and its own janitor. It is emptied from its own screen, never from here.
maintenance.notice_deferred_dangling_why: Designed for a later phase. Doing it right means subtracting the images running containers still reference, the ones every installed app's compose file names, and anything whose variables we could not resolve — and the Docker client lives in another service. Until all three subtractions exist, the number would be a promise we could not keep.
maintenance.notice_deferred_logs_label: Container logs that escape rotation (not implemented yet)
maintenance.notice_deferred_logs_why: Designed for a later phase. The fix is not deleting: log options are frozen when a container is created, so containers older than the current Docker config ignore it. The action worth shipping recreates those containers through our own compose flow — a button you press once instead of every month.
